questions.prompt: What unit is used to measure capacity (volume of a liquid)?

choices.feedback: cm is a unit of length, not capacity.
g is a unit of mass, not capacity.
m² is a unit of area, not capacity.

hints: Capacity measures how much a container can hold.
The standard units are litres (L) and millilitres (mL).
Think of a water bottle: it holds about 1 litre.
questions.explanation: Capacity is measured in litres (L) and millilitres (mL).

questions.prompt: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?

choices.feedback: 10 mL = 0.01 L. There are 1000 mL in 1 L.
100 mL = 0.1 L. There are 1000 mL in 1 L.
10 000 mL = 10 L. There are 1000 mL in 1 L.

hints: Think of a large bottle of water: it holds 1 L or 1000 mL.
questions.explanation: 1 litre = 1000 millilitres, because 'milli-' means one thousandth.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between litres and millilitres?

choices.feedback: 100 mL = 0.1 L. There are 1000 mL in 1 L.
10 mL = 0.01 L. There are 1000 mL in 1 L.

hints: Think: how many small containers of 1 mL fill a 1 L bottle?
questions.explanation: 1 litre = 1000 millilitres. Milli- means one thousandth, so 1000 millilitres make 1 litre.

questions.prompt: Why is capacity measured in cubic units (e.g., cm³) as well as litres?

choices.text: 1 cm³ is the same as 1 mL, so they are interchangeable
Cubic units are only used for solids, never liquids
choices.feedback: Capacity can be measured in either cm³ or mL (1 cm³ = 1 mL), so both are used.

choices.text: Cubic units are very rare and rarely used
choices.feedback: cm³ is commonly used for capacity; 1 cm³ = 1 mL.

choices.text: Only cubic units have been approved for Grade 4
choices.feedback: There is no such rule. Both cm³ and mL are used for capacity.

hints: 1 cm of water in a cube that measures 1 cm × 1 cm × 1 cm holds 1 mL.
This is why we can use both cm³ and mL for capacity.
questions.explanation: 1 cm³ = 1 mL, so cubic centimetres and millilitres are interchangeable. Both measure capacity.

questions.prompt: How many millilitres are in 3 litres?

choices.feedback: 3 L = 3000 mL. 300 mL would be 0.3 L.
3 L = 3000 mL. 30 mL would be 0.03 L.

questions.prompt: A jug contains 250 mL of juice. How many millilitres are in 4 such jugs?
Which holds more: a 2 L bottle or ten 250 mL cups?

choices.feedback: 10 × 250 mL = 2500 mL, which is more than 2 L.
10 × 250 mL = 2500 mL. This is more than 2 L (2000 mL).
We can compare: 2 L = 2000 mL, and 10 × 250 mL = 2500 mL.

hints: Convert to the same unit: 2 L = 2000 mL.
questions.explanation: 2 L = 2000 mL. Ten 250 mL cups = 10 × 250 = 2500 mL. The cups hold more.

questions.prompt: A container holds 1500 cm³ of water. What is its capacity in litres?

choices.feedback: 1500 cm³ = 1.5 L. 15 L would be 15 000 cm³.
1500 cm³ = 1.5 L. 0.15 L would be 150 cm³.
